> The OMNI stand is a compact, 3D-printable desktop organizer designed to eliminate cable clutter and streamline nightstand or workspace layout. It features a top-loading storage compartment where we can store all the things we wish to store. Directly behind the storage compartment is an integrated ergonomic vertical arm to hold my headphones.

## Design

### 2026-10-16 – # October 12: Base Block & Initial Layout

**5.5h**

# October 12: Base Block & Initial Layout

Started the OMNI Stand project in Onshape with the goal of designing a compact 120x120mm desktop charging station to organize my Galaxy Watch 8 and Sony WH-CH-720N headphones.

For this session, I created a center rectangle on the top plane, dimensioned it to 120mm x 120mm, and extruded it upward by 30mm to form the main solid base block. To give it a sleek, modern, and print-safe finish, I applied a 12mm fillet to all four vertical outer corners.

![Screenshot 2026-10-14 233027](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/MqfXtqzyoV3kC5NbjDzdPoc1zza7pyWb/82b6fccf5e8ceb9c3f9b4145a3be3929c53b1cb37d677820d938c886d8db9cd8.png)
**Total time spent: 1.5 hours**

---

# October 13: Watch Puck Recess & Rear Cable Slot

Next, I focused on integrating the smartwatch charging module. I created a new sketch on the top surface of the base and drew a 32mm circular profile custom-sized to fit the magnetic charging puck for the Galaxy Watch 8 (44mm).

Using the Extrude-Remove feature, I cut a 7mm deep pocket so the puck sits flush. I also added a rear drop-in cable slot (4mm wide) running from the back of the puck recess to the rear edge of the base, allowing the charging cord to be inserted or removed easily without fishing it through a closed tunnel.

![Screenshot 2026-10-14 233141](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/MqfXtqzyoV3kC5NbjDzdPoc1zza7pyWb/f0cb8360bdc3394953b9f2922b3c3c0c6a94ed616fbd38fa4d6324f80c7e8b33.png)

**Total time spent: 2 hours**

---

# October 14: Vertical Headphone Arm & Height Optimization

For the headphone stand component, I sketched a rectangular profile (25mm x 40mm) on the top surface behind the watch puck recess.

I initially tested an extrusion height of 180mm–190mm, but after checking the physical dimensions and minimum clearance required for the Sony WH-CH-720N over-ear headphones, I increased the vertical arm length to **245 mm** to ensure the earcups hang freely without hitting the desk. Finally, I applied fillets to the top edges of the arm to create a smooth, curved headband rest that prevents creasing or damage to the cushion.

![Screenshot 2026-10-14 234000](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/MqfXtqzyoV3kC5NbjDzdPoc1zza7pyWb/56cff4c993853a7ede6d4a02a538a89b1e9167129298b1953990479232625a44.png)

**Total time spent: 2 hours**

**October 18: Carving out the storage tray & mastering Onshape extrusions!!**

I finally got the base storage cutout working exactly how I wanted, and I figured it out completely on my own!

My original plan was to have a cut-out for a smartwatch charger, but I decided to pivot and turn the top of the 22 cm base into a clean, shallow valet tray for everyday desk items like keys, flash drives, and earbuds.

The main problem I ran into at first was handling the extrusions. When I tried to create the recess, Onshape kept trying to make a brand-new separate part (Part 2) floating in space instead of cutting a cavity straight into my main base block.

Here’s how I figured out the fix:

I realized I needed to use the Extrude tool's Remove operation rather than creating a new solid.

By sketching an inward Offset from the outer perimeter of the base, I locked in a uniform, premium border wall all the way around.

Total time spent: 2h

![Screenshot 2026-10-18 123159](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/MqfXtqzyoV3kC5NbjDzdPoc1zza7pyWb/118d285eba46ab0c6540f815c6445346236d1fe2c13828280f03c841ae95cc07.png)

### 2026-10-18 – # October 18: Perfecting the U-shaped cradle, color grading, & exporting!!

**3h**

# October 18: Perfecting the U-shaped cradle, color grading, & exporting!!

Today was all about finishing touches. After getting the base storage cutout sorted, I tackled the most important functional part of the stand: the top headphone cradle.

Originally, I was looking at a simple upward arch, but after sketching it out on paper, I realized a **U-shaped hook** would be way better. Designing a proper U-trough means the headphone headband drops right into a secure hollow space and won't ever slide off or get pinched.

![Screenshot 2026-10-18 173727](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/MqfXtqzyoV3kC5NbjDzdPoc1zza7pyWb/81070e12231b27fddcb7c48e8ba37e87e738de2dde2004e61563d52f8bacd24f.png)

Here’s how I dialed in the U-hook and wrapped up the model:
* **Shaping the Trough:** I used the side plane at the top of the 25 cm arm to sketch a clean, concave curve, offsetting it downward to give the hook solid wall thickness and slightly raised lips to lock the headband in place.

![Screenshot 2026-10-18 174557](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/MqfXtqzyoV3kC5NbjDzdPoc1zza7pyWb/56c8fd3be6e8dda3aa49ee7d162bde1a4cf67ca49f35d191ebfb8c2f12a0f680.png)

![Screenshot 2026-10-18 174611](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/MqfXtqzyoV3kC5NbjDzdPoc1zza7pyWb/9f776ddbb3d0c27b1cd6039ac76865b861c49bf25993896636640da7c03336c8.png)

![Screenshot 2026-10-18 174621](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/MqfXtqzyoV3kC5NbjDzdPoc1zza7pyWb/e4a54a92b4bd069ea942ba12e9d9a8569b0782f640b971ac909c9133c0d99d09.png)

* **Color Grading & Materials:** To get that high-end dual-tone aesthetic, I jumped into Onshape’s appearance panel. I set the base tray and the top U-cradle to a rich dark walnut brown (`#442809`), and gave the 50 mm wide vertical pillar a sleek matte black finish. The contrast looks incredible.
* **Final Cleanup & Export:** I pressed `P` to hide all the reference planes, double-checked the 22x22 cm base proportions, and got the model completely locked.

Here is how the final render came out on screen before exporting to .step:

![Screenshot 2026-10-18 182048](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/MqfXtqzyoV3kC5NbjDzdPoc1zza7pyWb/a52f5f7676617e9d9fd0d9b745ad398d1c30b5e95932753847daf97bff33f525.png)

Building this completely step-by-step—from a complex charger dock idea down to this minimalist valet tray and headphone stand hybrid—taught me a ton about Onshape workflows, extrusions, and managing multi-part assemblies.

**Total time spent: 3h**

### 2026-10-18 – # October 18: Slicing setup, export validation, & getting print-ready!!

**1h**

# October 18: Slicing setup, export validation, & getting print-ready!!

Today was the final wrap-up step before getting the OMNI stand ready for production. With the CAD model fully locked in—complete with the 22 cm base, recessed valet tray, matte black pillar, and walnut U-shaped cradle—it was time to transition everything into the slicer.

Here’s what I knocked out this session:
* **Exporting & File Prep:** I finalized the 3D model exports, ensuring both the `.step` source file and the print-ready `.stl` file were properly structured for the repository.
* **Slicer Configuration:** Loaded up the model into the slicer to simulate the print path and verify layer generation. I checked the orientation to make sure it prints flat on its base for optimal bed adhesion and structural rigidity.
* **Path & Layer Verification:** Simulated the toolpaths to ensure the 15% infill and solid wall settings would properly reinforce the 25 cm vertical arm without any weak spots around the U-cradle or the valet tray rim.

Everything is officially green-lighted, checked into the repo, and ready to print!

**Total time spent: 1h**
